key: The Master said, ‘He who speaks without modesty will find it difficult to make his words good.’
s: After judgements on princes and their ministers, the day’s passage closes on a saying about speech; He Yan’s collection, on 14.21, gives Ma Rong, who reads unashamed speech as coming from substance within, and the gathering of that substance as what is hard.

evidence.words: 馬曰：“怍，慚也。內有其實，則言之不慚。積其實者，為之難。”
evidence.gloss: Ma Rong says: zuo means to be ashamed. When one has the substance within, one speaks of it without shame. Accumulating that substance is what is hard to do.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Analects 14.21, at 352), the last unit of the day. The only jijie note on 14.21 is tagged 馬曰, so it is Ma Rong’s gloss and the sentence credits him through He Yan’s collection as the plan requires, not He Yan himself. His words carry the reading: unashamed speech comes from having the substance within, and gathering that substance is the hard part. This differs from Legge’s ‘without modesty’ and from Zhu Xi (大言不慚, boastful talk without resolve), and the sentence attributes only Ma Rong’s view, adding nothing of the translator’s. Plain sense faithful: 14.17 to 14.20 judge Duke Hwan, Kwan Chung, Kung-shu Wan’s minister and Duke Ling’s officers, and 14.21 closes day 14.
